text.p: Here are highlights of stories in Romania's press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
Business:
CAPITAL
- The state Tarom airiline is affected by serious financial problems, the paper says.
- Paging companies in Romania have 70,000 subscribers.
CURIERUL NATIONAl
- Interest rates will double the price of bread.
CURIERUL NATIONAL
- Tarom's general manager Dan Vulcan blamed the State Ownrship Fund (FPS) for allegedly delaying the privatisation of the airline.
ADEVARUL
- The World Bank gave Romania credits worth $550 million.
- The FPS is determined to go ahead with plans to restructure Tarom, the paper said.
General:
ROMANIA LIBERA

- Over 400 ethnic Germans who moved from Romania to Germany have sent a letter to Germany's President, Chancellor and Foreign Minister asking that the Bonn government support Romania in its bid for rapid admission to NATO, the paper reported.
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI
- The paper publishes a report on how late communist dictator Nicolae Ceausescu's daughter and son are living.
- The bill on returning assets of Romania's Jewish community was approved by a parliamentary commission.
CURIERUL NATIONAL
- American folk singer Joan Baez will have a live concert in Bucharest on June 22.
ADEVARUL
- Polish Foreign Minister Dariusz Rosati will start a one-day visit to Romania on June 12, the paper said.
- The Party of Social Democracy (PDSR), the main opposition party, will lodge a censure motion on Thursday, the paper report.
-- Bucharest newsroom 40-1 3120264
